q013ecd31.a: I first ask why the data is missing. Then I drop, impute with a median or model, or add a missing flag, depending on the reason. For outliers I check if they are errors or real, and use robust methods where needed. I record every choice.
q013ecd31.q: How do you handle missing data and outliers?
q013ecd31.w: Understand why it is missing, impute or drop, robust methods, document choices.

q025c74a4.a: EC2 gives virtual servers with full control. ECS and EKS run containers, ECS is simpler and EKS uses Kubernetes. Lambda runs code on events without servers and charges per execution. I choose based on control needed, traffic pattern and team skills.
q025c74a4.q: What is the difference between EC2, ECS, EKS and Lambda?
q025c74a4.w: Control vs convenience, cost model, when each fits.

q066671f4.a: First I look at the data: counts, types, missing values and duplicates. I handle missing values by removing, filling or flagging them depending on the reason. I remove duplicates, fix data types and spellings, check outliers against business logic, and keep a log of every change so the work can be repeated and explained.
q066671f4.q: How do you clean a messy dataset?
q066671f4.w: Missing values, duplicates, types, outliers, documenting every step.

q06dc6bf0.a: Smoke testing is a quick check that the build is stable enough to test further, for example login and the main page open. Sanity testing is a narrow check after a small fix to confirm that one change works. Regression testing re-runs a wide set of old tests to confirm that new changes did not break existing features. I run smoke on every build, sanity after a hotfix, and full regression before a release.
q06dc6bf0.q: What is the difference between smoke, sanity and regression testing?
q06dc6bf0.w: Define each in one line, then say when you run it in your pipeline.

q09900eb4.a: I follow the checklist, double check amounts, count cash twice, and reconcile at the end of the day. If I am unsure, I ask a senior before posting, because a corrected error costs more than a short question.
q09900eb4.q: How do you stay accurate with cash and numbers under pressure?
q09900eb4.w: Double check, follow the checklist, reconcile daily, ask when unsure.

q0ad615ff.a: If the customer is not happy with my answer or solution, I will ask them to hold the line and pass the call to a manager or team leader.
q0ad615ff.q: What if the customer is not happy with your answer or solution?

q0aef7a0e.a: My strengths are attention to detail, fast and accurate typing, time management and the ability to stay focused on repetitive tasks. I also have good communication skills for clarifying data-related issues.
q0aef7a0e.w: Change the years and tools to match your own real experience.

q0bf67a20.a: First, I will stay calm, listen to the customer's problem and try to understand what made them annoyed. Next, I will politely ask them to calm down. Then I will assure them that I will solve their problem. Last, I will find the root cause of the problem, fix it and make sure it does not happen again. Learning from the mistake can also improve the company's process and policy.
q0bf67a20.q: What will you do if a customer abuses you on the phone?

q0d652248.a: Yes, I would still work to build my career. With the lottery money, I will buy a big house for my mom and dad.
q0d652248.q: If you won a Rs 10 crore lottery, would you still work?

q0ddbf1e7.a: Org-wide defaults set the base access. Roles open up access up the hierarchy, and sharing rules extend it. Profiles and permission sets give object and field permissions, and field-level security hides fields. I design from least privilege and add access as needed.
q0ddbf1e7.w: Org-wide defaults, roles, profiles and permission sets, sharing rules, field-level security.

q0e7b17d3.a: I stay calm and polite. I speak slowly, use simple words and repeat the important points. I can ask, "May I confirm what you said?" If the process allows, I offer to continue in Hindi or another language they prefer, and if it still does not work I ask my team lead for help.
q0e7b17d3.h: Dheere bolo, aasaan shabd, dohrao. Process allow kare to Hindi mein poochho.
q0e7b17d3.q: The customer does not understand your English. What will you do?

q0ea9f10a.a: The box model says every element is content plus padding, border and margin. Flexbox lays items out in one direction, a row or a column, good for navbars and centering. Grid lays out rows and columns together, good for whole page layouts and card galleries. I often use grid for the page and flexbox inside components.
q0ea9f10a.q: What is the box model and how do flexbox and grid differ?
q0ea9f10a.w: One-dimensional vs two-dimensional layout with a use case each.

q102cf797.a: My biggest motivation is my family. They are my biggest source of inspiration and my strongest supporters. When I see my parents working, it gives me the drive to be like them. Their dedication motivates me.

q106da8a8.a: I set working agreements with overlap hours, use written async updates and a clear board, record decisions, and rotate meeting times so the burden is shared. Short, focused daily meetings and clear owners keep the team aligned.
q106da8a8.q: A distributed team across US and India time zones loses focus. What do you change?
q106da8a8.w: Overlap hours, async updates, clear working agreements, rotate meeting times.

q10813483.a: async and await let a method give up the thread while it waits for I/O, and the compiler turns it into a state machine that continues later. Calling .Result or .Wait() blocks a thread, and in a UI or older ASP.NET context it can deadlock. The fix is to await all the way up, and use ConfigureAwait(false) in library code.
q10813483.q: How do async and await work, and what goes wrong with .Result or .Wait()?
q10813483.w: State machine, no thread blocked, deadlock in sync contexts, ConfigureAwait.

q10b14682.a: ETL transforms data before loading it into the warehouse. ELT loads raw data first and transforms it inside the warehouse. Modern warehouses like BigQuery and Snowflake scale cheaply, so ELT keeps raw data available, is more flexible and lets analysts rerun transformations. ETL still helps when sensitive data must be cleaned before storage.
q10b14682.q: What is the difference between ETL and ELT?
q10b14682.w: Where transformation happens and why modern warehouses favor ELT.

q10c06740.a: Governor limits protect shared resources: for example 100 SOQL queries and 150 DML statements per transaction, CPU time and heap size limits. I hit the SOQL and DML limits most when code is not bulkified. The fix is to move queries and DML outside loops and work with collections.
q10c06740.q: Explain governor limits and name the ones you hit most.
q10c06740.w: SOQL queries, DML, CPU time, heap. Bulkify and avoid queries in loops.

q1115edc5.a: I define infrastructure in Terraform or CloudFormation, store code in Git, and use modules for reuse. Changes go through pull request review and CI runs plan before apply. State is stored remotely with locking, and I run drift detection to catch manual changes.
q1115edc5.q: How do you manage infrastructure as code?
q1115edc5.w: Terraform or CloudFormation, state, modules, review and CI, drift detection.

q11245cdc.a: "The first duty of cabin crew is the safety of passengers: the safety briefing, checking the doors and seat belts, and handling emergencies. The second is service: welcoming passengers, serving meals and keeping the cabin comfortable. We also help passengers who need special care and work as a team."
q11245cdc.h: Pehle safety (briefing, emergency), phir service (swagat, khana), phir passengers ko sambhalna.
q11245cdc.q: What are the main duties of cabin crew?
q11245cdc.w: Safety first (briefing, emergency, doors, seat belts), then service (welcome, meals, comfort), then handling passengers.

q11e7da6a.a: I create the catalog item with variables and variable sets, then use Flow Designer to add approvals and create fulfilment tasks. I set UI policies for dynamic fields and test with different roles, including rejection and rework paths.
q11e7da6a.q: How do you build a catalog item with approvals and fulfillment?
q11e7da6a.w: Variables, variable sets, workflow or Flow Designer, approvals, tasks, testing.

q12892c61.a: I check the match between ad and landing page, the offer and price, page speed on mobile, the audience, and whether conversion tracking works. Then I look for friction in forms or checkout. I change one thing at a time so I know what worked.
q12892c61.q: Your ads get clicks but no sales. What do you check?
q12892c61.w: Landing page, offer, audience, tracking, ad-to-page match, checkout friction. Fix one thing at a time.

q1302d570.a: I check the new request against the sprint goal and estimate its impact. I raise it with the product owner, who decides to swap it for something else or move it to the next sprint. If it must be added, it goes through a change request. I document it so scope is visible to everyone.
q1302d570.q: Scope creep is hitting the sprint. What do you do?
q1302d570.w: Impact analysis, change request, product owner decision, document it.

q133bc796.a: No, I do not have any problem with night shifts. Yes, I am willing to work on weekends.
q133bc796.h: Poora sentence mein jawab do. Sach boliye.
q133bc796.q: Are you willing to work night shifts or weekends?
q133bc796.w: Answer in a full sentence and be honest. If you have a limit, say it politely before joining.

q13a99e4e.a: "Good morning, Hotel [name], [my name] speaking. How may I help you?" I smile while speaking, speak slowly and clearly, note the message and repeat it to confirm. I end with "Thank you for calling."
q13a99e4e.h: "Good morning, Hotel [naam], main [aapka naam], kya madad kar sakta/sakti hoon?"
q13a99e4e.q: How do you answer a hotel phone call?
q13a99e4e.w: "Good morning, Hotel [name], [your name] speaking, how may I help you?" Smile, speak slowly, note the message.

q14805d87.a: I use walkthroughs and prototypes or wireframes so people react to something concrete. I send a written summary, collect feedback, update the document and ask for formal sign-off. After that, changes go through change control with impact on time and cost.
q14805d87.q: How do you validate requirements with stakeholders?

q1482173c.a: I look at the data first: estimation accuracy, scope added mid-sprint, interruptions, dependencies, work in progress and sprint goal quality. Then the team and I choose one experiment, such as smaller stories or reserved capacity, and check it in the next sprint.
q1482173c.q: The team keeps missing sprint goals. What do you look at?
q1482173c.w: Estimation, interruptions, dependencies, WIP, data from velocity and burndown.

q14c26b49.a: I use job portals like Naukri and LinkedIn, an applicant tracking system if the company has one, and Excel for trackers with formulas such as VLOOKUP, filters and pivot tables. I would also say which of these I really know.
q14c26b49.q: Which HR tools or Excel skills do you use?
q14c26b49.w: ATS, Naukri or LinkedIn, Excel for trackers, basic formulas like VLOOKUP.

q14d42521.a: I do not alert the customer. I follow the bank process, report it to my supervisor and the compliance or AML team, and document what I saw without opinions. I keep the information confidential.
q14d42521.q: You notice a transaction that looks suspicious. What do you do?
q14d42521.w: Do not tip off the customer, follow the process, report to the compliance or AML team, document.

q14ee9ddc.a: First I look at the data to find where users drop. Then I reduce steps, offer guest checkout, show total cost early, add trust signals and good error messages, and make forms short with the right keyboard type on mobile. I test the new flow with users and an A/B test.
q14ee9ddc.q: Redesign the checkout flow of a shopping app that has high drop-off.
q14ee9ddc.w: Find where users drop, reduce steps, guest checkout, trust signals, test the change.

q15686e2f.a: Sir, your company is well known for customer service, and you also have a great relationship with your customers.
q15686e2f.q: What do you know about our company?
q15686e2f.w: Visit the company website the day before and replace this sample with real facts: what the company does, one service or client, and where the office is.

q157789bc.a: I look at the cost explorer grouped by service, account and tag to find what grew. I check for idle or oversized resources, unattached volumes, extra data transfer and forgotten test environments. I ask the owner team, fix the waste, set budgets and alerts, and enforce tags for ownership.
q157789bc.q: Cloud costs doubled this month. How do you find out why?
q157789bc.w: Cost explorer, tags, top services, idle resources, ownership.

q17510602.a: HashMap stores entries in an array of buckets chosen by the hash of the key. Equal hash buckets hold a linked list of entries. Since Java 8, a bucket with many entries turns into a balanced tree, so worst-case lookup is O(log n) instead of O(n). It resizes when the load factor of 0.75 is crossed. It is not thread-safe; use ConcurrentHashMap for concurrent use.
q17510602.q: How does HashMap work internally? What changed in Java 8?
q17510602.w: Buckets, hashing, collisions, treeification, resize, thread-safety.

q180d5d02.a: A call centre is a service desk where the customer associate handles a large volume of calls to provide services to the client.
q180d5d02.q: What do you know about the call centre industry?

q19a24216.a: I assess the application, dependencies and database first. I add tests around critical behaviour, then migrate step by step with the strangler approach instead of a big-bang rewrite. I upgrade to modern .NET where possible, host on App Service or containers, and plan for rollback and data migration risks.
q19a24216.q: A client wants to move a legacy .NET Framework app to the cloud. How do you plan it?
q19a24216.w: Assess, strangler approach, upgrade path, tests first, containers or App Service, risks.

q1a9d935b.a: Example structure (use your own): "I worked on [project] as [module] consultant in a team of [n]. I handled [requirements, configuration, testing], and the result was [go-live date and result]." Be clear on your own contribution.
q1a9d935b.q: Tell me about an implementation you supported and your role.
q1a9d935b.w: STAR. Be clear on your module, team size, outcome.

q1c89047d.a: Waterfall suits stable, well-understood requirements with fixed scope, such as construction or compliance projects. Agile suits changing requirements where early feedback matters, such as software products. Often a hybrid works: fixed budget and milestones with agile delivery inside. I choose based on how stable the requirement is and how the client works.
q1c89047d.q: Agile vs waterfall: when do you use which?
q1c89047d.w: Requirement stability, feedback needs, team and client context.

q1eaddf7e.a: I listen to the constraint and ask what is hard. Then I offer a simpler version that keeps the user goal, and we agree on it together. I update the design and keep the notes clear so we do not repeat the problem.
q1eaddf7e.q: A developer says your design is hard to build. What do you do?
q1eaddf7e.w: Listen, understand the limit, find a simpler version, keep the user goal.

q20d57639.a: I choose the language the team already knows, for example Java with Selenium or TypeScript with Playwright, and a test runner like TestNG or Playwright Test. Structure: page objects, reusable helpers, test data layer, config per environment, and reports such as Allure. Tests run in parallel in CI, in a clean environment, with tags for smoke and regression. I start small with the critical flows, then grow it, and review flaky tests every week.
q20d57639.q: Design an automation framework from scratch for a new web product.
q20d57639.w: Language and tool choice, structure, reporting, CI, test data, parallel runs, how you would scale it.

q215aa3c4.a: I believe this job will build my confidence and improve my skills. I would love to grow with your company.
q215aa3c4.q: Why do you want this job?

q21d843ba.a: Workflow rules and Process Builder are older automation tools that Salesforce is retiring, and Flow is the current tool for most automation. I use Flow first. I choose Apex when logic is complex, needs high volume handling, or cannot be done declaratively.
q21d843ba.q: What is the difference between a workflow, Process Builder and Flow, and what do you use now?
q21d843ba.w: Flow is the current tool, say when Apex is still better.

q2220c083.a: Example (use your own): "I ran an Instagram page for [project] for [time]. I posted [x] times a week, and in [time] reach grew from [a] to [b] and I got [n] enquiries." Real numbers, even small, are better than big claims.
q2220c083.q: Tell me about a post or campaign you managed and its result.
q2220c083.w: Use real numbers even from a college or personal project: reach, leads, growth.

q22653e43.a: "Yes. I understand that repeated tasks are part of the job. I stay focused by working in a steady routine, taking my short breaks on time, and checking my work for accuracy. In my [study or work] I also did [repeated task] without losing focus."
q22653e43.q: Can you stay focused on repetitive work?

q226724cd.a: "Yes, I can stand for long hours. I keep my uniform neat, my hair and nails clean and I follow the grooming and hygiene rules of the hotel."
q226724cd.h: Haan. Safai, uniform, grooming ka dhyan.
q226724cd.q: Can you stand for long hours? Are you comfortable with a uniform and grooming rules?
q226724cd.w: Yes. Say you keep neat hair, clean nails, proper uniform, and good hygiene.

q22869ac2.a: Accuracy misleads when classes are imbalanced. I use precision, recall, F1 and PR-AUC, and choose by the business cost of errors: for fraud we may favour recall, for spam filtering precision. I also tune the threshold, not just the model.
q22869ac2.q: How do you choose evaluation metrics for an imbalanced classification problem?
q22869ac2.w: Precision, recall, F1, PR-AUC over accuracy, business cost of errors.

q232d55c9.a: "I would apologise and offer to keep the luggage safely, ask the guest to relax in the lobby with a welcome drink if the hotel allows, and tell the housekeeping team to prepare the room first. I would update the guest as soon as the room is ready."
q232d55c9.h: Sorry, saaman rakhwao, lobby mein baithao, drink do, room ready hote hi batao.
q232d55c9.q: A guest arrives early and the room is not ready. What do you do?
q232d55c9.w: Apologise, offer to keep luggage, a seat in the lobby, a welcome drink, and update them when the room is ready.

q233bf46d.a: I understand why they resist, then give training with real examples, use super users as champions, show the benefit for their daily work and offer support after go-live. I collect feedback and fix pain points quickly.
q233bf46d.q: Users resist a new SAP process. What do you do?
q233bf46d.w: Training, champions, show benefit, support after go-live.

q234a08bd.a: Honesty, loyalty and determination to achieve my team's target. or "Professionalism, growth and a healthy work-life balance."
q234a08bd.q: What are the three most important things for you in a job?

q2402e578.a: I run kubectl describe pod to see events and the last state, and kubectl logs --previous to see why the last container exited. I check wrong config or missing secrets, failing probes, out-of-memory kills from resource limits, and image or command errors. I fix the cause, redeploy and confirm that restarts stop.
q2402e578.q: A pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. Walk me through debugging.
q2402e578.w: describe, logs (previous), events, config, probes, resources.

q24cbb787.a: I open the browser network tab to see which request or file is slow, then check API timings, database queries and payload size. Differences from local are usually data volume, network, missing indexes or caching, and no CDN. I fix the biggest cost first and verify in production metrics.
q24cbb787.q: The page is slow in production but fast locally. How do you debug it?
q24cbb787.w: Network tab, API timings, DB queries, payload size, caching, CDN, then fix the biggest cost.

q24de4709.a: I explain the cost of mid-sprint change in terms the Product Owner understands, protect the sprint goal, and help improve backlog refinement so priorities are clearer before the sprint. We agree a rule, for example urgent changes swap with equal-sized work.
q24de4709.q: How do you coach a Product Owner who changes priorities mid-sprint?
q24de4709.w: Protect the sprint, explain cost of change, backlog refinement, agree a rule.

q25d5a37f.a: [Your town] is a [small town / city] in [your state]. It is a simple place where a person can live comfortably. We get education, markets, banks, a hospital and other facilities here, so it is a very suitable place to live.
q25d5a37f.h: [Brackets] mein apni jaankari daaliye. 4-5 aasaan sentences.
q25d5a37f.w: Replace the [brackets] with your own details. Keep it to 4-5 simple sentences.

q261e1002.a: I use semantic HTML (button, nav, label), make everything usable by keyboard with visible focus, give images alt text, keep colour contrast at the WCAG level, and use ARIA only when native elements are not enough. I test with a screen reader and an accessibility checker like axe.
q261e1002.q: How do you make a web app accessible?
q261e1002.w: Semantic HTML, keyboard, ARIA only when needed, contrast, screen reader testing.

q267514b2.a: I research the person and company first. My opener is short: "Hi [name], this is [me] from [company]. I saw [something specific], and I help companies like yours with [benefit]. Do you have two minutes?" Then I ask questions, listen, give one clear value point and agree a next step such as a demo or a call.
q267514b2.q: How do you cold call or message a new lead?
q267514b2.w: Research first, short opener, ask questions, give value, clear next step. Give a sample opening line.

q26bd27e9.a: Example (use your own): "I built [app] to [purpose]. It has [features], uses Kotlin, Room and Retrofit, and follows MVVM. A hard part was [problem], and I solved it by [fix]. It is on [Play Store or GitHub link]."
q26bd27e9.q: Tell me about an app you built or published.
q26bd27e9.w: Purpose, features, tech, a hard problem solved. Share a Play Store or GitHub link.

q26d58687.a: I measure first. tracemalloc or memory_profiler shows where memory is allocated. Common causes are loading whole files or query results into lists, caches that never expire and references kept in globals. Fixes: generators, chunked reads, pagination, __slots__ or a bounded cache. Then I confirm memory stays flat under load.
q26d58687.q: A Python service uses too much memory. How do you diagnose it?
q26d58687.w: tracemalloc, profilers, generators, chunking, leak patterns.

q26fefb30.a: I check the totals first, then look for transposition errors (for example 54 written as 45), entries posted on only one side, wrong amounts or ledger heads, and balances moved incorrectly. A difference divisible by 9 often points to a transposition. I review recent entries and temporary suspense accounts.
q26fefb30.q: Your trial balance does not tally. How do you find the error?
q26fefb30.w: Check totals, transposition errors, one-sided entries, suspense, review recent entries.

q271a2da1.a: "I want to become cabin crew because I enjoy serving people and making their journey comfortable. I know the first duty of cabin crew is the safety of passengers, and I like working in a team with responsibility. I am ready for the training and the discipline this job needs."
q271a2da1.h: Logon ki seva, safety, teamwork - sirf ghoomna ya glamour mat boliye.
q271a2da1.q: Why do you want to be cabin crew?
q271a2da1.w: Mention service to people, travel with responsibility, teamwork and safety. Avoid "I only want to travel and glamour".

q271f1fdc.a: Example (use your own): "Sales and operations wanted different approval rules. I held a short workshop, wrote both needs side by side with the cost of each, and showed data on how often each case happens. They agreed on a rule with an exception path. I documented the decision and got sign-off." The point is facilitation, not taking sides.
q271f1fdc.q: Tell me about a time stakeholders disagreed on requirements.
q271f1fdc.w: STAR. Focus on how you facilitated the decision.

q2756a3e8.a: Say your method, then an example. Example: "I list everything, mark urgent and important tasks, and agree the order with my manager. I finish the high impact work first, tell people early if something will slip, and avoid distractions. In [project] I handled [three tasks] in [time] this way and delivered on time."
q2756a3e8.q: How do you handle tight deadlines and many priorities?
q2756a3e8.w: A method plus an example with the result.

q28069aaf.a: Yes, I am quite organised. I keep all my documents, certificates and files labelled and sorted, so I can find anything in seconds. I also keep my computer desktop clean.

q28604f90.a: A savings account is for individuals with interest and limited free transactions. A current account is for businesses with many transactions and usually no interest. A fixed deposit locks money for a fixed period at a higher interest rate, with a penalty for early withdrawal.
q28604f90.q: Explain the difference between savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
q28604f90.w: Purpose, interest, withdrawals, who uses each.

q288ddf70.a: Once, I noticed that I had entered incorrect invoice data because of a formatting issue. As soon as I caught the mistake, I informed my supervisor, corrected the records and helped update the report before submission. Since then, I have been extra careful with formatting and use data validation rules wherever possible.
q288ddf70.q: Describe a time you made a mistake and how you handled it.
q288ddf70.w: Change the years and tools to match your own real experience.

q290c4980.a: MITRE ATT&CK is a public knowledge base of attacker tactics and techniques. I map my detection rules to it to see coverage and gaps, use it to plan threat hunting, and to describe incidents in a common language.
q290c4980.q: What is the MITRE ATT&CK framework and how do you use it?
q290c4980.w: Map detections to tactics, find gaps, threat hunting.

q2956a55b.a: I use AWS Organizations with separate accounts for production, non-production, security and logging. Service control policies set guardrails, a landing zone (Control Tower) standardises setup, and logs go to a central account. A network hub connects accounts, access is through SSO with roles, and a break-glass account is protected and monitored.
q2956a55b.q: Design a secure multi-account setup for an enterprise.
q2956a55b.w: Organizations, SCPs, landing zone, central logging, network hub, break-glass access.

q2994e2fa.a: I first understand the real business need behind the request. Then I explain the technical impact in simple words, with options and costs: the exact request, a simpler alternative, or a phased approach. I record the decision in writing. If the client still wants it, I raise the risk with my manager, but I do not just say no.
q2994e2fa.q: A client wants a feature that will hurt system design. How do you respond?
q2994e2fa.w: Understand the real need, present trade-offs, offer an alternative, document the decision.

q299cf6f9.a: I talk to five users, run a short survey, review competitors, study analytics if they exist, and run quick usability tests with a prototype on friends or target users. Even small tests show the biggest problems.
q299cf6f9.q: How do you do user research when you have no budget?
q299cf6f9.w: Talk to 5 users, surveys, competitor review, analytics, usability tests with friends.

q29e9f377.a: I was feeling exhausted after years of non-stop work, so I decided to take a break and spend time with my family. I am happy to have returned fully recharged.
q29e9f377.q: Why is there a gap in your work history?
q29e9f377.w: Be honest, short and positive. Then say you are ready to work.

q2a8537f0.a: "Sharp objects, lighters and flammable items are not allowed in the cabin bag, and large liquids are limited. Power banks have special rules, usually to be carried in the cabin bag. I would tell the passenger the rule politely and say it is for safety."
q2a8537f0.h: Tez cheezein, lighter, jwalansheel cheezein, bade liquid. Security rule ke hisaab se.
q2a8537f0.q: What items are not allowed in a cabin bag?
q2a8537f0.w: Sharp objects, lighters, flammable liquids, power banks in checked bag (rules apply), large liquids. Say "as per the security rule".

q2a92d006.a: I explain that every change affects time, cost and quality, and use a change control process: log the request, assess the impact, present options, and get written approval before work starts. I stay friendly and focus on the client's real goal, so changes are a managed decision and not a surprise.
q2a92d006.q: How do you handle a client who keeps changing scope?
q2a92d006.w: Change control, impact on time and cost, written approval.

q2acec76c.a: I start with a business requirements document or project brief, then stakeholder lists, process flows for as-is and to-be, user stories with acceptance criteria, wireframes, and a requirements traceability matrix. q2acec76c.w: BRD, user stories, process flows, wireframes, traceability matrix.

q2af9a39e.q: A passenger refuses to fasten the seat belt or switch off the phone. What will you do?

q2c99c7b7.q: What do you do if you see something suspicious or lost property?

q2ce04dfc.q: What is more important to you: work or money?

q2cf22758.a: I split documents into chunks, create embeddings in a vector store, retrieve the most relevant chunks and put them in the prompt. For reliability I write clear prompts, ask the model to cite sources, evaluate answers on a test set, add guardrails, and manage cost and latency with caching and a suitable model size.
q2cf22758.q: How do you build an LLM or RAG application and keep answers reliable?
q2cf22758.w: Chunking, embeddings, retrieval quality, prompts, evals, guardrails, cost and latency.

q2e2f7015.a: Firewalls separate security zones and enforce policies between them. NAT translates private addresses to public ones. VPNs create encrypted tunnels: site-to-site for offices and remote access for staff. I log traffic and review rules regularly.
q2e2f7015.q: How do firewalls, NAT and VPNs fit in a secure design?
q2e2f7015.w: Zones, policies, site-to-site and remote access, logging.

q2eca3ed2.a: He was very friendly with me. He inspired me a lot. I have always tried to learn something new from him.
q2eca3ed2.q: Can you tell us something about your previous boss?
q2eca3ed2.w: Say something positive and what you learned.

q2f2060d4.a: I check where the time goes: slow queries, N+1 queries, large images, and missing caching. I use the logs and a profiler, enable opcache, add caching for repeated results, and fix the largest delay first. Then I measure again.
q2f2060d4.q: A PHP page takes 8 seconds to load. How do you find the cause?
q2f2060d4.w: Profile queries, N+1, caching, opcache, image size, server logs.

q30b679be.a: A call centre is all about providing quality service to the customer. If you handle customers well and offer good service, you can be successful in a call centre.
q30b679be.q: What is the key to success in a call centre?

q31300514.a: First I find why it is flaky instead of adding retries. Usual causes are timing, unstable locators, shared test data and test order. I use explicit waits on conditions, stable locators such as data-test ids, and make every test independent with its own data. If a test is still flaky I quarantine it so it does not block the build, log a ticket, and fix the root cause within a set time.
q31300514.q: How do you handle flaky tests in Selenium or Playwright?
q31300514.w: Explicit waits, stable locators, test isolation, retries only as a last step, quarantine and root-cause.

q3145aefb.a: A call centre job means talking to customers, understanding their problem and helping them with the right solution.
q3145aefb.q: What is a call centre job according to you?
q3145aefb.w: The interviewer is checking whether you know the job. Talk about helping customers with their problems.

q316dd780.a: Example (use your own): "Sales were falling in one region. I compared it to other regions, found that a delivery delay was causing cancellations, and showed the numbers to the operations head. They changed the courier and cancellations dropped [x] percent." Always end with the number that mattered and the decision it changed.
q316dd780.q: Tell me about an analysis that changed a business decision.
q316dd780.w: STAR with the number that mattered.

q318e4258.q: Can you stand for long hours and wear a uniform?
q318e4258.w: Yes. Mention good fitness, neat grooming, and a polite attitude.

q32469cc1.q: The guest says the food is cold. What will you do?
q32469cc1.w: Apologise, take the dish back, tell the kitchen, serve a fresh dish, check again with the guest.

q33c03ffc.a: I would use a websocket for live updates, but throttle or batch the updates so the UI renders at a steady pace. For large tables or charts I use virtualization to draw only visible rows and keep state normalised. I also design loading, empty, error and reconnect states so the dashboard never looks broken.
q33c03ffc.q: Design the frontend of a real-time dashboard with large data.
q33c03ffc.w: State management, virtualization, websockets, throttling, error states.

q3459960e.a: I use REST messages or Integration Hub spokes for API calls, MID Server when the system is behind a firewall, and import sets with transform maps for data loads. I handle authentication, retries and error logging, and test with sample data first.
q3459960e.q: How do you integrate ServiceNow with another system?
q3459960e.w: REST messages, Integration Hub, MID server, import sets, transform maps, error handling.

q355f831f.a: I believe decisions should be made with all the information. If you miss an important detail, it is easy to make a bad decision. So I make important decisions after getting all the information.
q355f831f.q: How do you make important decisions?

q35643680.a: I write stories in the form "As a [user], I want [goal], so that [value]" and check them against INVEST: independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small and testable. Acceptance criteria use Given-When-Then, for example: Given a registered user, when they enter a wrong password three times, then the account is locked for 30 minutes.
q35643680.q: How do you write good user stories and acceptance criteria?

q3646b72c.a: I define churn clearly, for example no purchase in 90 days, build features from behaviour and billing, avoid leakage by using only data available before the churn date, and train a model. I use precision and recall and agree with the business what action follows for high-risk customers.
q3646b72c.q: How would you predict customer churn?
q3646b72c.w: Define churn, features, leakage, model, metrics, how the business acts on it.

q380106c5.a: The GIL lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time in CPython. So threads do not speed up CPU-heavy work. For CPU-bound jobs use multiprocessing or native libraries like NumPy. For I/O-bound work like API calls or file reads, threads or asyncio work well because they wait most of the time.
q380106c5.q: What is the GIL and how does it affect concurrency?
q380106c5.w: CPU-bound vs I/O-bound, threads vs processes vs asyncio.

q3935f353.a: KYC (Know Your Customer) means the bank verifies the identity and address of a customer with documents. It is required by RBI rules to prevent fraud, money laundering and misuse of accounts, and it must be kept up to date.
q3935f353.q: What is KYC and why is it required?
q3935f353.w: Know Your Customer: identity and address proof, prevents fraud and money laundering, RBI rules.

q3aafdb84.a: LWC is the modern framework with web standards, and Aura is older. Components communicate down with public properties, up with custom events, and across the page with Lightning Message Service. They get data with the wire service or call Apex methods. I prefer LWC for new work.
q3aafdb84.q: Lightning Web Components vs Aura: how do they communicate?
q3aafdb84.w: Properties, events, LMS, wire service, Apex calls. Say you prefer LWC.

q3acd367b.a: Example (use your own): "I enjoy helping people and I like that HR affects both employee experience and company results. During [college or project] I [helped organise something or support people], and I found I like it. I want to learn recruitment and employee relations and grow in HR."
q3acd367b.q: Why do you want a career in HR?
q3acd367b.w: People interest, helping both employees and company. Give a real reason, not 'I like people' only.

q3bcbf944.a: My name is [your name]. I am from [your city]. I have completed my [10th / 12th / graduation] in [your stream]. I learn quickly and I am a good listener. I want to start my career in [this role] and grow with your company.
q3bcbf944.h: Naam, shehar, padhai, ek skill aur is job ki wajah bataiye. Dheere aur saaf boliye.
q3bcbf944.w: Use 4-5 short sentences: name, city, studies, one skill, why you want this job. Speak slowly and clearly.

q3d457e7a.a: I watch heap usage and GC logs to confirm heap keeps growing. Then I take a heap dump with jmap or on OutOfMemoryError, and open it in Eclipse MAT or VisualVM to see which objects are retained and by what. Common causes are static collections that never clear, unclosed resources, listeners not removed and ThreadLocals. I fix the reference, add a test or a metric, and watch heap after deployment.
q3d457e7a.q: How would you find and fix a memory leak in a production Java service?
q3d457e7a.w: Heap dump, GC logs, profilers, typical causes (static maps, listeners, thread locals).

q3d87ec04.a: I start with out-of-the-box features and configuration, because custom code raises upgrade cost and risk. I explain the cost of each customisation to the business, offer a configuration option, and document the decision if we still customise.
q3d87ec04.q: The business asks for heavy customization. How do you respond?
q3d87ec04.w: Out-of-the-box first, upgrade cost, configuration over code, document the decision.

q3e004afe.a: First, check if rollback is the fastest safe step, since users are affected. Look at the dashboard for error rate and the logs for the stack trace, and compare with what changed in the deployment: code, config, database migration. Tell the team and stakeholders a short status. After the service is stable, I find the root cause and write a short post-incident note with the prevention step.
q3e004afe.q: A production API is returning 500 errors after a deployment. Walk me through your first 15 minutes.
q3e004afe.w: Check rollback option, logs, metrics, recent change, communicate status.

q3e11a022.a: The main channels are SEO, paid search and display ads (SEM), social media marketing, email marketing, content marketing and affiliate marketing. I would say which I have actually worked on, for example "I managed Instagram content and ran a small Facebook ad".
q3e11a022.q: What are the main channels of digital marketing?
q3e11a022.w: SEO, SEM or paid ads, social media, email, content, affiliate. Say which you have actually worked on.

q3e1ceaaf.a: I automate tests that are repeated often, stable, high risk and data heavy, such as login, checkout, API contracts and cross-browser checks. I do not automate one-time tests, features that change every sprint, or visual judgement checks. I compare the time saved against the cost of writing and maintaining the script, and start with the smoke and regression core.
q3e1ceaaf.q: How do you decide which test cases to automate?
q3e1ceaaf.w: Repeatable, stable, high-risk, data-heavy flows first. Mention ROI and maintenance cost.

q402b8e6b.a: My mother is [name]. She is a [occupation]. She always took good care of me. We have a very close connection, and I love her very much.
q402b8e6b.h: [Brackets] mein apni jaankari daaliye. 4-5 aasaan sentences.
q402b8e6b.w: Replace the [brackets] with your own details. Keep it to 4-5 simple sentences.

q40e3fae3.a: "Many hotels have check-in around 12 noon or 2 PM and check-out around 11 AM or 12 noon, but it differs by hotel. I would follow the policy of the hotel where I work and tell the guest politely."
q40e3fae3.h: Hotel ke hisaab se badalta hai - policy follow karo.
q40e3fae3.q: What is the usual check-in and check-out time?
q40e3fae3.w: Many hotels use 12 or 2 PM for check-in and 11 AM or 12 noon for check-out (varies by hotel). Say you would follow the hotel policy.

q40fa22ee.a: Example structure: the problem and metric, the data and its limits, a simple baseline, features and models tried, validation method, final result in business terms (for example "reduced churn by [x] percent"), and what I would improve. Choose a real project of yours.
q40fa22ee.q: Explain a model you built end to end and how you chose it.
q40fa22ee.w: Problem, data, baseline, features, validation, result in business terms.

q415f0b29.q: Are you comfortable with irregular shifts, nights and being away from home?
q415f0b29.w: Say yes if true. Mention family support and that you will manage rest and health.

q41857754.a: I use rolling updates with readiness probes so traffic only goes to healthy pods, and set maxUnavailable to zero. For riskier changes I use blue-green or canary releases with a small percentage of traffic first. I keep the previous version for quick rollback and watch error rate and latency during the release.
q41857754.q: How do you do zero-downtime deployments in Kubernetes?
q41857754.w: Rolling update, readiness probes, blue-green or canary, rollback.

q433d7a34.a: I start with a simple baseline they understand, show where the model is right and wrong honestly, and explain the main drivers in plain language. I involve them early and let them test it on cases they know.
q433d7a34.q: A stakeholder does not trust your model. How do you win them over?
q433d7a34.w: Explainability, simple baseline, show errors honestly, involve them early.

q438fb7e1.a: REST is simple, cacheable and widely understood, with one endpoint per resource. GraphQL lets the client ask for exactly the fields it needs in one request, which avoids over-fetching, but adds complexity in caching and security. I choose REST for simple CRUD and GraphQL when many clients need different data shapes.
q438fb7e1.q: REST vs GraphQL: when do you pick each?
q438fb7e1.w: Over-fetching, caching, tooling, team skills, a real example.

q43954429.a: Upselling means offering the guest something better or extra so that they enjoy more, for example a better room or a meal combo. Example: "Sir, would you like a room with a sea view for a small extra amount?" It must always be honest and not forced.
q43954429.h: Guest ko behtar room ya service suggest karna. Example: "Sea-view room lena chahenge?"
q43954429.w: Offering a better room, a meal combo or a service so the guest enjoys more. Example: "Would you like a sea-view room for a little extra?"

q4535be4c.a: I rate my communication skills around 8 out of 10. I am improving every day by speaking and listening in English.
q4535be4c.q: How do you rate yourself on communication skills?
q4535be4c.w: Call centres look for good communication, so rate yourself high but honestly, and mention how you improve.

q457185b4.a: An ACL checks table, field or record access by operation, role, condition and script, and all must pass. I debug with the Security Debugger or by impersonating a user to see which rule blocks access, then adjust the minimal rule.
q457185b4.q: How do ACLs work and how do you debug one?
q457185b4.w: Table, field, role, condition, script; security debugger.

q45ad7ae0.a: I stay calm and reproduce the failure myself. I share logs, screenshots, the exact steps and the expected result from the requirement. If it is truly a test problem, I fix it quickly and thank them. If it is a bug, I show the evidence and sit with the developer for ten minutes to debug together. The goal is a correct product, not winning the argument.
q45ad7ae0.q: Developers say your failing test is a test problem, not a bug. What do you do?
q45ad7ae0.w: Reproduce, share evidence, pair on it, stay factual and calm.

q46fd95b2.a: Example (use your own): "I use SQL for extracting and checking data, Excel for quick analysis, Power BI for dashboards, and Python for cleaning large files. In [project], I used SQL and Power BI to show [result]." Choose one real project per tool and say what decision it supported.
q46fd95b2.q: Which tools have you used (Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Python) and for what?
q46fd95b2.w: Be specific about one project per tool.

q49df3a24.a: "I would check who booked first and be fair and honest with both guests. If I cannot give the room, I would offer another date or another nearby hotel and tell my manager so they can decide."
q49df3a24.h: Booking dekho, imaandaari se, alternative, manager ko batao.
q49df3a24.q: Two guests want the last available room. What will you do?
q49df3a24.w: Check booking priority, be fair and honest, offer another hotel or date if needed, tell your manager.

q4a507ee1.a: "The baggage allowance depends on the airline and the ticket. If a bag is overweight, I politely tell the passenger the excess baggage charge as per the airline rule, or suggest they take out some items."

q4a507ee1.q: What is the baggage allowance? What if a bag is overweight?

q4bfa9f1e.a: No. I can work with all kinds of people. I focus on the work and respect everyone.
q4bfa9f1e.q: Is there any particular kind of person you cannot work with?

q4cc71fbb.a: I break my tasks into smaller goals and take short breaks to stay focused. I also use keyboard shortcuts and templates to speed up repetitive work. I enjoy routine work and take pride in staying consistent.
q4cc71fbb.q: How do you handle repetitive work without losing focus?
q4cc71fbb.w: Change the years and tools to match your own real experience.

q4ce4637a.a: I use JWT or OAuth with policies for authorization, version the API in the URL or header, and support pagination and filtering. For load I use caching, async calls, rate limiting and a scalable database. I add health checks, structured logging and monitoring, validation, and clear error responses.
q4ce4637a.q: Design a Web API for orders with auth, versioning and high load.
q4ce4637a.w: JWT or OAuth, versioning, pagination, caching, rate limits, health checks, logging.

q4d2d1a05.a: I check counters like CPU, GC collections and memory with dotnet-counters, take a dump with dotnet-dump or use a profiler, and analyse what is retained. Common leaks are event handlers never unsubscribed, static caches and undisposed objects. I fix, then verify memory is stable under load.
q4d2d1a05.q: How do you find a memory or CPU problem in a production ASP.NET service?
q4d2d1a05.w: Counters, dotnet-dump or profiler, GC behavior, common leaks like event handlers.

q4e6ae2c1.a: Example (use your own): "In my college event I helped guests find their seats and supported my team. The event ran smoothly. I enjoy helping people and I learned that teamwork makes work easy."
q4e6ae2c1.h: Chhoti kahani: aapne kya kiya, natija.
q4e6ae2c1.q: Tell me about a time you worked in a team or helped someone.
q4e6ae2c1.w: A short story from school, college, an event or home: what you did and the result.

q4e9fb4d1.a: Example (use your own): "During my exam the paper was very hard and I felt panic. I took a deep breath, did the easy questions first, and finished well. I learned that staying calm helps me think clearly."
q4e9fb4d1.h: Exam ya emergency ka chhota example, aur seekh.
q4e9fb4d1.q: Can you stay calm in a stressful situation? Give an example.
q4e9fb4d1.w: A short story where you stayed calm (exam, a crowd, a family emergency). End with what you learned.

q4ea184c2.a: My long-term goal is to become a respectable and successful person.

q4fcb447b.a: When state or props change, React re-runs the component, compares the new virtual DOM with the old one and updates only what changed. useMemo caches an expensive calculation and useCallback caches a function so child components do not re-render needlessly. I use them only after measuring a real slowdown, because they add complexity.
q4fcb447b.q: How does the React rendering cycle work? When do you use useMemo or useCallback?
q4fcb447b.w: State change, reconciliation, avoid premature optimization, measure first.

q5079695f.a: "I would speak kindly to the child and offer water, a toy or a colouring sheet if available. I would also help the parents relax and ask if they need anything. I would stay patient and calm."
q5079695f.h: Pyaar se baat, paani/khilona do, parents ko comfortable karo.
q5079695f.q: A child is crying and the parents are stressed. What do you do?
q5079695f.w: Speak kindly, offer water/toy/colouring if available, help the parents settle, stay patient.

q50db2777.q: What is smart work and what is hard work?

q51d13539.q: Where do you see yourself in 3 years?
q51d13539.w: Supervisor or senior executive, after learning the work well.

q51da182f.a: I open Cost Explorer grouped by service, account and tag to see what grew. I look for idle or oversized resources, unused volumes, data transfer and forgotten test environments, then rightsize or delete. I add budgets and alerts, tag standards, and consider savings plans for steady workloads.

q51da182f.w: Cost Explorer, tags, find top services, rightsizing, savings plans, guardrails and alerts.

q52f21476.q: Are you comfortable with shifts, night duty and holidays?

q52fcd967.a: I package the model with its preprocessing, serve it through an API or batch job, version the model and data, and automate tests and deployment in CI/CD. In production I monitor latency, errors and prediction quality, and keep a rollback to the previous version.
q52fcd967.q: How do you take a model from notebook to production?
q52fcd967.w: Packaging, API, versioning, CI/CD, monitoring, rollback.

q53072322.a: First I check data quality: a broken pipeline or a changed definition. Then I split the KPI by dimension: region, device, product, channel, customer type, and by time to see where the drop started. I compare with releases, campaigns and outside events. I report the cause with numbers and a suggested action.
q53072322.q: A KPI dropped 20% this week. How do you investigate?
q53072322.w: Check data quality first, segment by dimension, time, release, external events.

q53e2a18d.a: Success is most important to me, because money follows success. For example, players, singers and runners earn money wherever they succeed.
q53e2a18d.q: What is more important to you: money or success?

q555eb2ed.a: N+1 happens when code runs one query for a list and then one more for each item. I use Include or projection with Select to fetch what is needed in one query, AsNoTracking for read-only queries, and add indexes. I check the generated SQL and execution plan.
q555eb2ed.q: Entity Framework: how do you avoid N+1 queries and slow queries?
q555eb2ed.w: Include/projection, AsNoTracking, indexes, look at the generated SQL.

q55f47861.a: The main modules are FI (finance), CO (controlling), MM (materials management), SD (sales and distribution), PP (production planning) and HCM. They integrate: a goods receipt in MM posts to FI, and a sales invoice in SD posts to FI. I would describe my own module and its links.
q55f47861.q: What are the main SAP modules and how do they integrate?
q55f47861.w: FI, CO, MM, SD, PP, HCM and the S/4HANA view. Pick your module and show the links.

q55fba993.a: I tell the CFO's team early that I am on it with a time estimate. I trace the lineage from the report back to the source to find where the number went wrong, fix and reload, and verify with a reconciliation against the source totals. Then I add a check so it does not happen again.
q55fba993.q: The finance report is wrong and the CFO is waiting.
q55fba993.w: Triage the lineage, communicate early, fix and prevent.

q56a1b477.a: "Yes. I have read the airline's requirements for height, weight in proportion, vision and grooming, and I meet them. I will bring all my documents and I am ready for the medical check." Answer honestly - if something does not fit, say you will check the rule.
q56a1b477.h: Rules airline ke hisaab se badalte hain (height, weight, aankhein). Padhkar sach batao.
q56a1b477.q: Are you comfortable with height, weight and medical rules for this job?
q56a1b477.w: Rules vary by airline (minimum height, weight in proportion, vision, no visible tattoos). Say you have read the rules and fit them. Be honest.

q577fa0fb.a: It starts with the requirement and a job description, then sourcing, screening, interviews, selection and offer, background verification and onboarding. I follow up with candidates between offer and joining to reduce drop-off, and keep a backup candidate.
q577fa0fb.q: Explain the recruitment process from requirement to joining.
q577fa0fb.w: JD, sourcing, screening, interviews, offer, background check, onboarding. Mention drop-off handling.

q58d59483.a: Functional requirements say what the system does, for example "a user can reset a password by email". Non-functional requirements say how well it does it, for example "pages load in under 2 seconds" or "supports 5,000 users at once". Other examples: security, availability, accessibility. Both must be testable.
q58d59483.q: What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements?
q58d59483.w: Give two examples of each from a real project.

q59845f1f.a: I get easily frustrated with people who do not work hard. But I know people have different work styles and habits. So if I could change something, I would like to be more understanding.
q59845f1f.q: If you could change one thing about your personality, what would it be?

q5a1469f6.a: ECC runs on any database, while S/4HANA runs on the in-memory HANA database with a simplified data model (for example Universal Journal in finance) and the Fiori user interface. Migration can be greenfield, brownfield (system conversion) or selective.
q5a1469f6.q: What is the difference between ECC and S/4HANA?
q5a1469f6.w: In-memory HANA, simplified data model, Fiori, migration approaches.

q5a1e4453.a: The browser looks up the domain through DNS, opens a TCP connection and TLS, and sends an HTTP request. The server or CDN returns HTML, the browser parses it, loads CSS, JavaScript and images, builds the DOM and renders the page. Then JavaScript calls APIs, which hit the backend and database. I can explain where I would measure delays at each step.
q5a1e4453.q: Walk me through what happens from typing a URL to seeing the page.
q5a1e4453.w: DNS, TCP/TLS, request, server, response, render. Show you know both sides.

q5b5f6cca.a: Back office: the part of the company with employees doing administrative and support work. They do not deal directly with customers but are the backbone of the company. Example: in a bank or finance company, managing and settling accounts, clearing payments, updating records, running IT infrastructure, data entry and HR. The back office does not generate revenue, but the front-office sales team cannot complete a deal without its support. Front office: people who deal directly with customers, such as sales and customer support. They generate revenue. Back-office staff work behind the scenes, execute the deals sales brings in and take them to completion. Both offices must work hand in hand.

q5bbb7de4.a: An idempotent pipeline gives the same result if it runs twice. I use deterministic keys, upserts or MERGE instead of blind inserts, and overwrite the partition being processed. I keep checkpoints, so a failed run can be restarted safely without duplicates.
q5bbb7de4.q: How do you design an idempotent pipeline?
q5bbb7de4.w: Deterministic keys, upserts, replay safely, checkpointing.

q5ca51a66.a: I use data like velocity to show what is realistic, explain the trade-off between more scope, quality and date, and offer options such as a smaller first release. I protect the team from overcommitment, while staying respectful and clear with management.
q5ca51a66.q: Management wants the team to commit to more than it can deliver.
q5ca51a66.w: Use data, show trade-offs, protect the team, offer options.

q5ca67bdb.a: For structured data I use Room (SQLite). For small settings I use DataStore (or SharedPreferences for old code). For files, I use internal storage. I never store passwords in plain text.
q5ca67bdb.q: How do you store data locally?
q5ca67bdb.w: Room, SharedPreferences or DataStore, when to use each.

q5ccaa991.a: I keep one trigger per object that calls a handler class. The handler works on lists of records (Trigger.new), uses sets and maps to query once, and does one DML for all changes. No SOQL or DML inside loops. I test with 200 records at a time.
q5ccaa991.q: How do you write a bulk-safe Apex trigger?
q5ccaa991.w: One trigger per object, handler class, collections, maps, no SOQL or DML in loops.

q5cd362ab.a: I keep enough colour contrast, readable font sizes, touch targets of about 48 px, visible focus states and labels for fields. I do not rely on colour alone to show meaning and I think about keyboard and screen reader use.
q5cd362ab.q: How do you make a design accessible?
q5cd362ab.w: Contrast, font size, touch targets, labels, keyboard use, do not rely on color alone.

q5cfc10a1.a: Example: "Before I sell it, may I ask how often you write, and what you look for in a pen?" Then link a feature to their answer: "You sign many documents, so this smooth ink does not smudge and the grip stops hand tiredness." Handle one objection, then close: "Shall I pack one for you or would you like two?" Asking questions first is the key.
q5cfc10a1.q: Sell me this pen (or any product).
q5cfc10a1.w: Ask about their need first, then link features to benefits, handle one objection, close with a clear ask.

q5d0dd59d.a: Example (use your own): "My most memorable day was when I [passed my exam or got first prize or helped my family]. I felt proud and happy because of my hard work. It motivates me to work hard in my career too." Keep it positive and short.
q5d0dd59d.q: What is your most memorable day / happiest moment so far?

q5dd798af.a: I vary the format so it stays fresh, create safety so people speak honestly, and end with one or two actions that have owners and a date. At the next retrospective we first review those actions, so the team sees change really happens.
q5dd798af.q: How do you run a retrospective that produces real change?
q5dd798af.w: Format variety, one or two actions with owners, follow up next sprint.

q617ae24f.a: Answer honestly: "Yes, I can travel daily. My home is about [distance] from the office and it takes me [time]. I can also use the company cab if available." If travel is a problem, say it truthfully and say what you can do.
q617ae24f.h: Doori aur time sach batao. Cab ho to bolo.
q617ae24f.q: Can you travel to the office daily?

q61f7bdd4.a: "I would apologise and take the passenger to the baggage service desk. We would fill the lost baggage report and give the passenger the reference number and a way to track it. I would assure them we will follow up."
q61f7bdd4.h: Sorry, baggage desk par le jao, report bharo, reference number do.
q61f7bdd4.q: A passenger's bag did not arrive. What will you do?
q61f7bdd4.w: Apologise, take them to the baggage service desk, fill the lost-baggage report (PIR), give the reference number.

q628143d9.a: I start with research and the goal, define personas and user flows, sketch wireframes, build a clickable prototype, test with real users, and iterate. Then I hand off the design with specs, states and assets, and review the build with the developers.
q628143d9.q: Walk me through your design process.
q628143d9.w: Research, personas, wireframes, prototype, test, iterate, hand-off.

q6337c7eb.a: "I would listen carefully and apologise. I would note the room number and send housekeeping at once, or offer another clean room. After the work is done I would call or visit the guest to confirm they are satisfied."
q6337c7eb.h: Suno, sorry, room number note, housekeeping bhejo ya room badlo, baad mein poochho.
q6337c7eb.q: A guest complains that the room is not clean. What will you do?
q6337c7eb.w: Listen, apologise, note the room number, send housekeeping fast or change the room, follow up after.

q64f49d25.a: MVVM separates the View (UI), ViewModel (state and logic) and Model (data). The ViewModel survives rotation and does not hold a reference to the UI, so the logic is easier to test and the code stays clean.
q64f49d25.q: What is MVVM and why use it?
q64f49d25.w: Separate UI and logic, survives rotation, easier testing.

q657ab359.a: The pipeline runs smoke tests on every commit, API and integration tests on merge, and full regression nightly or before release. A build is blocked if smoke or critical tests fail. Flaky tests are quarantined by a clear policy so they do not block everyone. Results go to a dashboard and the team channel, and the owner of the failing change is notified.
q657ab359.q: How do you run automation in CI/CD and decide when a build is blocked?
q657ab359.w: Quality gates, test levels per stage, flaky policy, reports, who gets notified.

q674caf5c.a: Value types such as int and structs hold the data directly, usually on the stack. Reference types such as classes hold a reference to an object on the heap. Boxing wraps a value type into an object, which allocates memory and costs time. Example: storing ints in an old ArrayList boxes each one; List<int> avoids it.
q674caf5c.q: Explain value types vs reference types and boxing in C#.
q674caf5c.w: Stack vs heap in simple terms, boxing cost, a case where it hurt performance.

q68594a46.a: Example (use your own): "I am [name] from [city], I completed [course]. I enjoy talking to people and I like that in sales my effort shows in my results. In [college or part-time work] I [sold or promoted something], and I learned to listen first. I want to start my career in sales and grow into a strong business development role." Keep it short and energetic.
q68594a46.q: Tell me about yourself and why sales?
q68594a46.w: Short story, show energy and target mindset, link any college or part-time selling experience.

q69397317.a: I use batching, quantisation, distillation or pruning, caching of frequent results, and route easy requests to smaller models. I measure latency and cost per request before and after to confirm the gain without hurting quality.
q69397317.q: How do you reduce inference cost and latency?
q69397317.w: Batching, quantization, distillation, caching, smaller model routing.

q698f57b1.a: "I would say no politely and explain the rule in a friendly way, for example 'I am sorry sir, our policy does not allow this because of safety'. I would offer an alternative that I can do and ask my senior if needed."
q698f57b1.h: Politely na, rule samjhao, alternative do, senior se poochho.
q698f57b1.q: A guest asks for something that is against hotel policy. What do you say?
q698f57b1.w: Say no politely, explain the rule, offer an alternative, and ask a senior if needed.

q6a488c3c.a: Example: "My strength is [reliable follow-through or quick learning], for example [one proof]. My weakness was [a real, small one such as speaking up in meetings]. I fixed it by [specific steps], and now [progress]." Choose a real weakness that does not block the job, and show the steps.
q6a488c3c.q: What is your biggest strength and a weakness you are fixing?
q6a488c3c.w: Real weakness plus concrete steps and progress.

q6c381a23.a: I define the hypothesis and one primary metric, calculate the sample size and duration in advance, and split users randomly. After the test I check that groups are balanced, then the statistical significance and the practical size of the change. A significant but tiny change may not be worth shipping. I do not stop the test early because the result looks good.
q6c381a23.q: How would you design an A/B test and read the result?
q6c381a23.w: Hypothesis, metric, sample size, duration, significance vs practical impact.

q6c843f16.a: A BPO (Business Process Outsourcing) organisation performs a process, or part of a process, for another business. Outsourcing is done to save cost or gain productivity. A call centre performs the part of a client's business that involves handling telephone calls, for example customer complaints. So a call centre can be considered a BPO.
q6c843f16.q: What is the difference between BPO and a call centre?

q6cc1c304.a: PF (provident fund) is a retirement saving to which employee and employer contribute. ESI is health insurance for employees under a salary limit. Gratuity is a payment for long service. A salary slip shows earnings (basic, allowances) and deductions (PF, tax). I always follow company policy and current labour law, and check the rules before answering an employee.
q6cc1c304.q: What are PF, ESI, gratuity and the basics of a salary slip?
q6cc1c304.w: Basic idea of each in simple words. Say you will always follow the company policy and labour law.

q6dab8c86.a: OSPF is an interior gateway protocol using link state, with fast convergence, used inside an organisation. BGP is an exterior protocol that exchanges routes between autonomous systems, used with ISPs and for multi-homing, and it is policy driven.
q6dab8c86.q: How do OSPF and BGP differ, and where do you use each?
q6dab8c86.w: IGP vs EGP, metrics, convergence, typical designs.

q6e4d5f19.a: "I would apologise sincerely and stay calm. I would offer the best alternatives available, like another meal or a drink, and ask my senior crew if more options are possible. I would thank the passenger for understanding and check again later that they are comfortable."
q6e4d5f19.h: Sorry bolo, shaant raho, doosra option do, senior crew ko batao.
q6e4d5f19.q: A passenger is angry because the meal they ordered is finished. What will you do?
q6e4d5f19.w: Apologise, stay calm, offer alternatives, ask a senior crew, thank them for understanding.

q6e7104a3.a: To handle a pressure situation, I keep my focus on work and avoid frustration. or "I have worked under pressure a lot during my college days. I have realised that I actually work well under pressure. The pressure brings out maximum efficiency in me."
q6e7104a3.q: How do you handle work pressure?

q6f7bf8e0.a: I monitor input feature distributions and prediction outputs, and compare with the training data using statistics like PSI. When thresholds are crossed, I alert and retrain or review. I use shadow deployments or A/B tests before replacing a model.
q6f7bf8e0.q: How do you detect and handle data drift and model decay?
q6f7bf8e0.w: Monitor inputs and outputs, thresholds, retraining triggers, shadow runs.

q6fb2b5d7.a: I define scope and goals, break the work into a WBS with milestones, estimate with the team, and list risks and dependencies. I track progress with a plan in a tool like Jira or MS Project, daily standups, a weekly status report and a clear risk log. I re-forecast when the plan changes.
q6fb2b5d7.q: How do you plan a project and track progress?
q6fb2b5d7.w: Scope, WBS, milestones, risks, a status cadence and tool.

q6fc5e89f.a: Success makes me happy. I also feel happy after completing my tasks and achieving my goals. Holidays with my family also make me happy.

q6fe64450.a: Layer 1 physical (cables, hubs), 2 data link (switches, MAC, VLAN), 3 network (routers, IP), 4 transport (TCP, UDP), 5 session, 6 presentation (encryption, encoding), 7 application (HTTP, DNS). I use it to isolate problems, starting from the bottom.
q6fe64450.q: Explain the OSI model and where common devices and protocols sit.
q6fe64450.w: Layers 1 to 7 with real examples: switch L2, router L3, TCP L4.

q71ce183c.a: I am looking for better growth and more learning opportunities. I am thankful for what I learned at my last company.
q71ce183c.q: Why did you leave your last job?
q71ce183c.w: Never speak badly about a past employer. Talk about growth.

q727052c4.a: 1. Greet the customer. 2. Introduce yourself. 3. Ask how you can help. 4. Listen patiently. 5. Give the best possible solution. 6. Cross-check that the customer is satisfied. 7. Ask if they need any further help.
q727052c4.q: What procedure do you follow while talking to a customer?

q73c81651.a: "I want to work in the hotel industry because I enjoy serving guests and making them feel welcome. I also want to learn and grow in a field with many opportunities. I want to start at the ground level and become a supervisor in future."
q73c81651.h: Guest ki seva aur seekhna pasand hai. Sirf tips/khane ke liye nahi.
q73c81651.q: Why do you want to work in the hotel industry?
q73c81651.w: Say you enjoy serving guests and learning. A good start for a long career. Not "only for tips or free food".

q74e55b51.a: Roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers. Events: Sprint, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective. Artifacts: Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Increment, each with its commitment (Product Goal, Sprint Goal, Definition of Done).
q74e55b51.q: What are the Scrum events, roles and artifacts?
q74e55b51.w: Name them briefly and the purpose of each.

q78a8c863.a: I measure first with Lighthouse and the Core Web Vitals. Then I reduce bundle size with code splitting and tree shaking, lazy load routes and images, compress and size images properly, use caching and a CDN, and avoid blocking scripts. I check the metrics again after each change.
q78a8c863.q: How do you improve page load performance?
q78a8c863.w: Bundle size, lazy loading, images, caching, Core Web Vitals.

q78fadae9.a: My father is [name]. He is a [occupation]. He is a simple and caring man. He cares about our family very much, and I love him very much.
q78fadae9.h: [Brackets] mein apni jaankari daaliye. 4-5 aasaan sentences.
q78fadae9.w: Replace the [brackets] with your own details. Keep it to 4-5 simple sentences.

q7947fe46.a: I first understand why it changed and the impact on design, development, testing and the date. I prepare two or three options with cost and time, such as accepting the change with a later date, a phased delivery, or keeping the old plan. I get written approval of the chosen option from the client before the team starts.
q7947fe46.q: A client changes a core requirement two days before UAT.
q7947fe46.w: Assess impact, options with cost and date, get written approval.

q79a84cda.a: I land raw data from each source into object storage with a standard format and metadata. An orchestrator like Airflow schedules ingestion, with schema validation and evolution rules. Processing writes partitioned Parquet tables to the warehouse. I add monitoring on volume and freshness, retries, and cost controls like lifecycle rules.
q79a84cda.q: Design a pipeline that ingests 1 TB per day from many sources.
q79a84cda.w: Ingestion, landing zone, schema evolution, orchestration, monitoring, cost.

q79d67bec.a: I have mainly worked with Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets and company CRM systems. I also have basic experience entering data into ERP systems and handling scanned documents with OCR software.
q79d67bec.q: What software or tools have you used for data entry?
q79d67bec.w: Change the years and tools to match your own real experience.

q7a1fb3fe.a: IATA stands for International Air Transport Association. Airport codes are three letters, for example DEL for Delhi, BOM for Mumbai, BLR for Bengaluru, CCU for Kolkata and HYD for Hyderabad.
q7a1fb3fe.h: IATA airline ka international sangathan hai. DEL, BOM, BLR jaise 3-letter codes.
q7a1fb3fe.q: What is IATA? Do you know any airport codes?
q7a1fb3fe.w: IATA = International Air Transport Association. Three-letter airport codes: DEL (Delhi), BOM (Mumbai), BLR (Bengaluru), CCU (Kolkata), HYD (Hyderabad).

q7a2e212c.a: I test on a real mid-range phone and use throttled network and CPU in dev tools. I look for long JavaScript tasks, large images and fonts, many requests and layout shifts. I fix the biggest cost first, for example smaller images and less JavaScript, and measure again on the device.
q7a2e212c.q: Users report the app is slow only on mobile. How do you investigate?
q7a2e212c.w: Real-device profiling, network throttling, long tasks, images, JS cost.

q7a836280.a: Good listening skills, problem-solving, concentration and patience.
q7a836280.q: What qualities should a customer associate have to be a perfect customer associate?

q7b34eda9.a: I would definitely consider it. If the opportunity is appropriate, rewarding and feasible, I do not think I will have any issue with relocation or travel.
q7b34eda9.q: Are you willing to relocate or travel?

q7b3ee9b2.a: First I find the root cause: estimation, scope growth, resources or dependency. Then I list options: cut or defer low-value scope, add people only where it helps, work in parallel, or move the date. I give the client a clear recovery plan with trade-offs early, and re-baseline with agreement. I never hide the delay.
q7b3ee9b2.q: A project is 30% behind schedule. What are your options?
q7b3ee9b2.w: Root cause, re-baseline, scope cut, resources, honest client conversation.

q7b5c368a.a: Number of repeat customers. Number and type of complaints. Number of referrals from current customers. Sales figures, if the service is product based. Customer satisfaction surveys. Benchmarking against competitors. Rate of new customers enrolling. Number of returns.
q7b5c368a.q: How do you measure good customer service?

q7b637896.a: Answer honestly. Example: "I can type well and I know MS Word, Excel and email. I have not used the airline booking system yet, but I am a quick learner and will learn it during training."
q7b637896.h: Jo aata hai bolo. Booking system training mein seekh loge.
q7b637896.q: Can you work on a computer? Do you know MS Office or any airline software?
q7b637896.w: Say what you know (typing, Word, Excel, email). Say you will learn the booking system in training.

q7c1625bd.a: I stop loading the whole file. I stream it line by line or in chunks with a generator or pandas chunksize, process and write results as I go, and keep a checkpoint so a rerun can continue. I also add error handling for bad rows and log the progress.
q7c1625bd.q: Your script processes a 10 GB file and crashes. What do you change?
q7c1625bd.w: Stream, chunk, avoid loading all in memory, checkpoint.

q7db9325d.a: GST is a tax on supply of goods and services, where the business pays the output tax collected less the input tax credit on purchases. GSTR-1 reports outward sales and GSTR-3B is the summary return with tax payment. I reconcile with books and the auto-generated purchase statement and file before the due dates as per current rules.
q7db9325d.q: What is GST and how do you file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B?
q7db9325d.w: Output and input tax, return purpose and due dates, reconcile with books and 2B.

q7dc68599.a: I collect metrics, logs and traces. I define SLOs such as availability and latency and alert on symptoms users feel, not on every small spike. Alerts have clear owners and runbooks to reduce noise. Dashboards show the golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and saturation.
q7dc68599.q: How do you monitor a production system?
q7dc68599.w: Metrics, logs, traces, SLOs, useful alerts vs noise.

q7dd275cb.a: "You should hire me because I have a good service attitude, I stay calm under pressure and I work well in a team. I am ready to learn, follow the safety rules, and be a positive face of your airline." Smile at the end.
q7dd275cb.h: Teen baatein: service ka bhav, pressure mein shaant, team player.
q7dd275cb.w: Three points: service attitude, calm in pressure, team player. Smile at the end.

q7e7371d3.a: Yes, I am willing to work long hours when the project demands it.
q7e7371d3.q: Are you willing to work long hours if the project demands it?
q7e7371d3.w: Answer in a full sentence. Be honest about your limits.

q7edb5c42.a: Give two specific reasons. Example: "The role uses [skill] which I enjoy and have practised in [project]. I also like that [company] works on [product or field] and gives a chance to learn [thing]. I read about [one real fact about the company], and I believe I can contribute from the first month." Do not mention only salary.
q7edb5c42.q: Why do you want this role and this company?
q7edb5c42.w: Two specific reasons about the work, not only salary.

q80c26158.a: I add tests at each stage: schema checks, not-null and unique checks, value ranges, row count reconciliation and freshness checks. I use tools like Great Expectations or dbt tests, alert on anomalies, and name an owner for each dataset. Bad records go to a quarantine table, not silently dropped.
q80c26158.q: How do you ensure data quality?
q80c26158.w: Tests, schema checks, freshness, anomaly alerts, ownership.

q813b7113.a: Partitioning splits a large table into parts by a key such as date or region. Queries that filter on that key scan only the needed partitions, which saves time and cost. I choose the key from the most common filters, and avoid keys with too many tiny partitions.
q813b7113.q: What is partitioning and why does it matter?
q813b7113.w: Prune data scans, choose key by access pattern.

q8150d3d7.a: "I would ask kindly what help they need, arrange a wheelchair and inform the staff. I would walk with them to the gate, help with the boarding and thank them."
q8150d3d7.h: Pyaar se poochho, wheelchair arrange, gate tak saath.
q8150d3d7.q: A passenger with a wheelchair or an elderly person needs help. What do you do?
q8150d3d7.w: Ask kindly, arrange the wheelchair, tell the staff, walk with them to the gate, thank them.

q81aec05c.a: I review my pipeline and focus on the hottest leads first, follow up everyone who showed interest, and ask my manager for support on one or two big deals. I plan the daily calls and meetings needed to close the gap, and I stay honest with customers - no false promises to hit the number.
q81aec05c.q: You are behind your monthly target with a week left. What do you do?
q81aec05c.w: Review pipeline, focus on hot leads, follow up, ask for support, stay ethical. Show a plan with numbers.

q821ccdbd.a: I use the SIEM to collect logs, build correlation rules and dashboards, and investigate alerts by searching across sources. A big part of the job is tuning rules to reduce false positives, and documenting playbooks for each alert type.
q821ccdbd.q: How do you use a SIEM such as Splunk or Sentinel day to day?
q821ccdbd.w: Correlation rules, tuning false positives, dashboards, investigations.

q8280fb75.a: "If I am not selected, I will thank the panel and ask for feedback. I will work on what I need to improve and apply again. I believe each interview is a learning chance."
q8280fb75.h: Feedback loge, sudhaar karoge, phir apply karoge.
q8280fb75.q: What will you do if you are not selected this time?
q8280fb75.w: Say you will ask for feedback, improve and apply again. Shows positive attitude.

q82ae5b95.a: I listen to both separately and stay neutral, collect the facts and follow company policy. I may hold a joint conversation to agree on a solution, document it, and follow up later. If it is serious, such as harassment, I escalate to the proper committee.
q82ae5b95.q: Two employees have a serious conflict. How do you handle it?
q82ae5b95.w: Listen to both separately, stay neutral, find facts, follow policy, document, follow up.
